name: Poulet nyembwe
subtitle: Poulet nyembwe is smoked chicken cooked in a palm-nut sauce, also called sauce graine.

facts.label: Status
facts.value: A traditional dish of Gabon, often considered the national dish.

facts.label: Main ingredients
facts.value: Mainly smoked chicken cooked in a palm-nut sauce, also called sauce graine.

facts.label: Name
facts.value: Nyembwé means palm oil in Myènè, a Bantu language spoken in Gabon.

facts.label: How it is cooked
facts.value: The smoked chicken pieces go in once the palm-nut sauce starts to thicken.

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: The dish comes from the Myènè people.

facts.label: How it is eaten
facts.value: Usually served with plantain, rice, cassava or yam purée.

parts.text: Poulet nyembwe is smoked chicken cooked in a palm-nut sauce, also called sauce graine. Nyembwe means palm oil in Myènè, a Bantu language of Gabon, and the dish comes from the Myènè people. It is often considered Gabon's national dish.
It is usually served with plantain, rice, cassava or yam purée.
